title: Executive QBR briefs + Renewal Risk Matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, exec-facing QBR deck template set + companion renewal risk matrix and playbook notes intended for fast turnarounds (24–48h prep) when the AE/CS team needs to escalate to an executive sponsor. The goal is to provide two concise variants: a 6-slide Lightning Brief for short exec syncs and a 12–15 slide Enterprise Brief for full QBRs with renewal/expansion decisioning.

Audience:
- Exec sponsor (VP+/C-level) 
- Customer Success Manager (CSM) and Account Executive (AE) 
- Solutions/Implementation lead (as needed)

How to use this doc (notes to self):
- Copy the appropriate slide outline into the deck maker and fill in baseline metrics.
- Use the Lightning Brief when renewal < 90 days and churn risk is <= medium; use Enterprise Brief for complex renewals, > $500k ARR, or legal/ procurement involvement.
- Highlight a single topline ask (e.g., decision on commitment level, funding for pilot expansion, approval for dedicated capacity purchase).
- Keep language action-oriented. Execs want one decision and supporting evidence.

Variant A — Lightning Brief (6 slides / 10 min):
1) Title + Ask (one sentence: renewal window, ask, impact) — one-sentence speaker note
2) Quick health summary (NPS / usage trend / latency SLA compliance) — 2 bullets
3) Key wins & blockers (2 wins, 1 blocker with mitigation)
4) Renewal math (current ARR, suggested options, delta) — table of 3 options
5) Risk elevator (renewal risk score + top 2 risk drivers)
6) Call to action + next steps / owners

Speaker notes (Lightning):
- Start with the ask. Then a one-line value reminder. If asked for more, expand with slide 3/4.
- If there is a technical blocker, have the SRE/solutions owner on the line or a rapid follow-up scheduled.

Variant B — Enterprise Brief (12–15 slides / 25–40 min):
1) Title / Agenda / Decision needed
2) Exec summary (1-paragraph value statement + ask)
3) Customer health dashboard (usage, latency, error rate, retention labels)
4) Adoption by team / product area (user cohorts, feature adoption rate)
5) Business impact (cost savings, time-to-value examples, internal ROI stories)
6) Support & reliability history (major incidents, MTTR, open bugs impacting deal)
7) Contract & commercial options (detailed pricing matrix + options)
8) Renewal timeline & procurement blockers (legal, security assessments)
9) Risks & mitigations (detailed risk matrix with owners)
10) Roadmap alignment & new capabilities (what’s coming that matters)
11) Migration / rollout plan for expansion (phases, minimum success criteria)
12) Ask / decision & fallback if not approved
13) Appendix: metrics definition table, logs/trace snapshot, open tickets

Renewal Risk Scoring Rubric (use for both variants):
- Score 1–10, where 1 = very low risk, 10 = imminent churn. Compose as sum of four 0–3 factors + 0–1 override: 
  - Usage trajectory (0 = steady/growing, 1 = slight dip, 2 = moderate decline, 3 = steep decline)
  - Value realization (0 = direct ROI, 1 = some ROI, 2 = unclear ROI, 3 = no value realized)
  - Relationship/engagement (0 = exec sponsor engaged, 1 = customer champion, 2 = passive, 3 = disengaged)
  - Procurement/legal friction (0 = none, 1 = routine, 2 = prolonged review, 3 = open blocking requests)
  - Override (0 or 1): 1 if key competitor is actively replacing or a budget cut is confirmed

Risk bands (example):
- 0–2: Green (low risk)
- 3–5: Yellow (monitor / tactical intervention)
- 6–8: Orange (CS+AE action plan required)
- 9–10: Red (exec escalation + retention package)

Renewal Friction Heatmap (one-pager to include in appendix):
- Columns: Procurement, Security, Budget, Product Fit, Exec Sponsorship, Support History
- Rows: Severity (None / Low / Medium / High)
- Populate quickly with color-coded cells and a single line action for each high/medium cell (owner + 48h next step).

Playbook excerpts (tactical scripts):
- If Risk >= 6 and procurement friction = High -> Immediate AE+CSM+Legal sync within 48h; propose a limited-time pilots/credit to buy time.
- If Usage drop > 30% month-over-month -> Schedule a 30m product adoption workshop with product solutions owner; propose a 6-week reactivation program.
- If performance regressions are present -> Offer priority SRE diagnostics + temporary SLA credit; capture post-mortem within 7 days.

Slides: content guidance and copy snippets:
- Title/ask slide: "Ask: Approve renewal at $X/year to preserve dedicated capacity and achieve Y% cost/perf improvement. Decision by DATE."
- Health slide header: "Overall health: GREEN / YELLOW / RED — primary driver: <usage|ops|procurement>"
- Risk elevator: short bullet: "Score 7 (Orange): procurement review + exec disengaged; recommended: exec touchpoint + 3-month bridge credit."

Annex: sample 3-option renewal table (copy into slide 4 Lightning / 7 Enterprise)
- Option A (Renew as-is): Term, Price, Notes
- Option B (Committed capacity discount): Term, Price, Benefit, Commitment level
- Option C (Upsell pilot): Short term pilot to expand footprint, pilot price, success metrics

Operational checklist before the QBR (48–24h):
- Confirm exec sponsor availability and agenda (AE)
- Pull last 90-day usage & errors (CSM / telemetry dashboard)
- Validate open tickets and mitigation timelines (Support Owner)
- Update renewal options spreadsheet and check margins (Finance ops)
- Create one-page Lightning Brief for exec calendar invite if time boxed

Common objections and quick scripts:
- Objection: "We didn’t get value from X feature" -> Script: "I hear you — we can schedule a targeted enablement session within 2 weeks to get your team to adoption and measure impact. Also propose a 6-week success metric to evaluate ROI."
- Objection: "Price is too high" -> Script: "We have a compressed option (pilot / committed capacity) that lowers per-token cost while preserving performance. Let me share a 3-option proposal and walk through the tradeoffs."

Appendix ideas (to clip into deck as needed):
- SLA performance charts (90d)
- Top 5 errors by volume with recent mitigations
- Adoption cohort table (teams, DAU, top features)
- Payment/contract timeline & gating checklist

TODOs (working items):

- [ ] Add automatic export of risk score from Salesforce renewal record into to this appendix (ACTION: Ravi)
- [ ] Draft one-pager for procurement play (ACTION: Emily)

Notes to presenter:
- Keep the first 90 seconds focused on the ask and business impact. Executives need the framing and a clear yes/no.
- If the meeting pivots to technical details, move to the appendix and assign a short follow-up where the tech owner owns the remediation plan.

Version history / context:
- Born out of a pilot with three large enterprise accounts Q2–Q3 2025; consolidated best-practices from CS, Solutions, and Legal.
- Intention: reduce time-to-decision and standardize escalation language.
